cards.text: Paul is writing a letter to the believers in Colossae (Col 1:1-2). He just told them they've been made complete in Christ, and that God canceled the debt against them by nailing it to the cross (Col 2:10, 14). Now he says “Therefore,” and friend, when Paul says therefore, that's the oven timer going DING.

cards.question: So Paul tells the Colossians: let no one ___ you by what you eat or drink.
Paul doesn't stop at food and drink. True or false: he also says not to let anyone judge you with regard to a Sabbath.

cards.text: Then Paul calls all of that a shadow of the things to come. Friend, I spent YEARS in a junk drawer, and not ONE shadow in there ever stamped a cookie.

cards.question: Paul calls food, drink, feasts, New Moons and Sabbaths a shadow of the things to come. Who does the body that casts that shadow belong to?

cards.text: Next, Paul warns about someone who delights in false humility and the worship of angels. False humility is the guy who says, “I'm the MOST humble person you will EVER meet. Ask anybody.”

cards.question: Paul warns about someone who delights in false humility and the worship of angels. Don't let him ___ you with speculation about what he has seen.
True or false: Paul says the person who delights in false humility is puffed up by a very spiritual mind.

cards.text: Then Paul shows this guy's real problem with a picture of a body. Friend, it's like a lamp that looks great on the table, but the cord is just lying on the floor.

cards.question: Paul says the person who delights in false humility has lost connection to the ___.

cards.text: From the head, the whole body is supported and knit together by its joints and ligaments. Like dough mixed just right, friend: every bit holding on to every other bit.

cards.question: In Paul's picture of a body knit together from the head, who causes the body to grow?

cards.text: Then Paul asks the Colossians a question. If you have died with Christ to the spiritual forces of the world, why live as though you still belonged to the world?

cards.question: Paul asks why, if they died with Christ to the spiritual forces of the world, they still submit to the world's ___.

cards.text: Here's how those rules sound: “Do not handle, do not taste, do not touch!” Friend, I have met smoke alarms with more chill than that.

cards.question: Paul looks at those “Do not handle, do not taste, do not touch!” rules. What does he say these will all do with use?
What does Paul say those “Do not handle” rules are based on?

cards.text: Paul admits these restrictions have an appearance of wisdom, with their self-prescribed worship, their false humility and their harsh treatment of the body. Looks wise, SOUNDS wise, got a whole wise outfit on.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says these restrictions are of real value against the indulgence of the flesh.
